_description: MOMENT Single Source of Truth for all Clinical Thresholds, Odds Ratios, and Medical Decision Limits

blood_pad_cv_severity_bands.source: UNVERIFIED HEURISTIC - EXPERIMENTAL ONLY. No peer-reviewed optical 2D saturation percentage cutoff exists in WHO/FIGO literature. WHO/FIGO only validate gravimetric pad weighing (1g = 1mL) or calibrated drapes (e.g. BRASSS-V). These thresholds (Routine <20%, Amber 20-55%, Critical >=55%) are calibrated engineering surface coverage heuristics across test pads (1.2% light lochia, 54.9% moderate watch, 96.0% heavy critical PPH) to trigger mandatory bedside vital checks.
blood_pad_cv_severity_bands.status: UNVERIFIED HEURISTIC - DO NOT CLAIM CLINICAL TRIAL VALIDATION IN DEMO
blood_pad_cv_severity_bands.note: This is a SURFACE SATURATION severity signal only. Explicitly NOT a volumetric (mL) estimate. Must always ship with the disclaimer: '2D image saturation cannot determine 3D absorption volume.'

shock_index.source: El Ayadi AM, Nathan HL, Seed PT, et al. / Miller PLoS One obstetric cohort (Dryad DOI: 10.7272/Q6MS3QNX, n=952 active low-resource obstetric hemorrhage patients). Verified empirical test characteristics: SI >= 0.9 (Sensitivity 100.0%, Specificity 4.60% for adverse outcomes); SI >= 1.4 (Sensitivity 89.47%, Specificity 69.04%, NPV 99.37% for mortality / critical intervention); SI >= 1.7 (Sensitivity 68.42%, Specificity 88.51%).
shock_index.last_verified: 2026-09-11 by User & Antigravity on raw ElAyadiMiller_PLoSOneSIPaper.dta

blood_loss_thresholds_ml.source: World Health Organization (WHO) Guidelines for the Management of Postpartum Haemorrhage and Retained Placenta (WHO 2012 / 2018 update): Postpartum Hemorrhage defined as blood loss >= 500 mL within 24 hours postpartum; Severe Postpartum Hemorrhage defined as blood loss >= 1000 mL.
blood_loss_thresholds_ml.last_verified: 2026-09-11 against WHO Guidelines & FIGO 2022 PPH Global Guidelines

bleeding_velocity_ml_per_min.source: Obstetric Critical Care & Massive Transfusion Guidelines (Baskett TF, 2019; French College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists / CNGOF Sentilhes et al. 2016): Persistent active continuing blood loss > 20 mL/min represents dynamic refractory hemorrhage outstripping physiological compensation, warranting immediate second-line medical/surgical intervention.
bleeding_velocity_ml_per_min.last_verified: 2026-09-11 against CNGOF & Obstetric Critical Care Literature

anemia_risk_multiplier.source: NFHS-5 India (National Family Health Survey 2019-21), IAIR7EFL.DTA, linked maternal birth cohort N=169,334 (variables s443_1 x v457). Multivariable logistic regression controlling for maternal age, parity, ANC visits, and delivery setting.
anemia_risk_multiplier.status: INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED TWICE WITH EXACT MATCH
anemia_risk_multiplier.note: Do NOT use the Assam cohort OR=9.0 as the live multiplier without clearly labeling it as a separate, small single-hospital cohort figure, distinct from the NFHS-5 national estimate.

postpartum_monitoring_protocol.critical_window_description: Fourth Stage of Labor: The immediate 2 hours postpartum represents the highest risk period for maternal mortality due to primary PPH, with uterine atony accounting for 70% to 80% of all primary PPH cases (WHO 2018, FIGO 2022, OpenStax Maternal-Newborn Nursing).
postpartum_monitoring_protocol.source: WHO Recommendations for Postpartum Care (2018) & NHM (National Health Mission) Dakshata Labour Room Quality Improvement Protocol: Mandates uterine tone, pulse, BP, and bleeding checks every 15 minutes during the first 2 hours post-delivery.
postpartum_monitoring_protocol.last_verified: 2026-09-11 against NHM Dakshata & WHO Postpartum Guidelines
